scope: Colorectal carcinoma predictive/prognostic biomarkers. Internal substrate only.

biomarker_records.scoring: Loss of one or more MMR proteins by IHC; MSI-high by molecular testing. Universal testing recommended on all colorectal cancers.
biomarker_records.therapy_linkage: MSI-H/dMMR gates immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy (including first-line in metastatic disease) and identifies Lynch syndrome candidates (esp. with MLH1/PMS2 loss prompting BRAF/MLH1-methylation reflex).
biomarker_records.companion_dx_basis: Checkpoint inhibitor trials in dMMR CRC; Lynch screening guidelines

biomarker_records.scoring: Expanded RAS testing (KRAS and NRAS exons 2/3/4).
biomarker_records.therapy_linkage: RAS mutation predicts LACK of benefit from anti-EGFR antibodies (cetuximab/panitumumab); only RAS wild-type tumors are candidates.
biomarker_records.companion_dx_basis: Anti-EGFR therapy trials / FDA companion dx

biomarker_records.therapy_linkage: Adverse prognosis; gates BRAF-inhibitor-based combination (with anti-EGFR) in metastatic disease. Also used as a reflex (with MLH1 methylation) to triage MLH1-loss tumors away from Lynch.

biomarker_records.scoring: CRC-specific HER2 scoring criteria (distinct from breast/gastric).
biomarker_records.therapy_linkage: HER2-amplified RAS/BRAF wild-type metastatic CRC gates HER2-directed therapy.

biomarker_records.scoring: Fusion present vs absent; enriched in MSI-H/MLH1-methylated tumors.
biomarker_records.therapy_linkage: Gates tumor-agnostic TRK inhibitors; rare but actionable.
Post-surgical ctDNA positivity is a strong recurrence predictor and is being used to guide adjuvant-therapy decisions (active trial area). A core Liquid Pulse topic.
biomarker_records.companion_dx_basis: MRD ctDNA studies (e.g., DYNAMIC and successors)

notes: Universal MMR/MSI testing + expanded RAS + BRAF is the core CRC panel. The MLH1-loss -> BRAF V600E / MLH1-methylation reflex is a high-value diagnostic-algorithm article. ctDNA MRD is the strongest Liquid Pulse crossover among the six cancers. Verify therapy linkages at write time.
